summary: Week 6 leans heavily toward unders and toward fading thin favorites. Several games pair top defenses with bottom offenses or backup and limping quarterbacks: Jackson and Mayfield are out, and Lock, Williams and Penix are uncertain. Early forecasts show gusty systems in London, Tampa, Kansas City and especially Lambeau (gusts near 39 mph). They are hedged mentions only, but they nudge those unders and argue against the passing overs we cut.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: Seattle has the better point differential (+5.8 vs -2.8 a game) and net EPA (11th vs 19th), and its defense ranks 2nd against a Denver offense ranked 24th. Denver's best unit, a pass defense ranked 3rd, is without both starting corners, Surtain and Moss. Denver's 3-2 record rests on a perfect one-score record that the efficiency doesn't support.
picks.risk: Lock's forearm. A limited or replacement QB behind an offense ranked 26th, with a run game 30th in rush EPA, may not score enough to win by 3.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Two top-seven defenses (SEA 2nd, DEN 7th in EPA allowed) face two bottom-nine offenses (DEN 24th, SEA 26th) on a Thursday short week. Denver has gone under in 4 of 5 and topped 20 points only once. Seattle's QB and top receiver are both limited, and the forecast is calm (gusts 15).
picks.risk: Denver's missing corners let Seattle's passing game hit explosives, or turnovers hand out short fields.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: The line implies about 19 for Denver, whose offense ranks 24th in EPA and 23rd passing. Against top-six defenses it scored 20, 14 and 23. Seattle's defense ranks 2nd in pass and rush EPA and 2nd in QB-hit rate, and takes away explosives, leaving Nix to dink.
picks.risk: Seattle turnovers (-0.4 a game) gift short fields, as happened against SF.

picks.bet: Nix under 20 rushing yards (his career-pace mark)
picks.label: Nix rushing yards
picks.case: Nix is averaging 7 rushing yards a game, hasn't topped 10 in any game, and has scrambled four times. Seattle ranks 2nd in rush EPA allowed. A number shaded toward his 21-25 career pace sits well above what he is doing this year.
picks.risk: One designed keeper or a broken-play scramble of 15+ yards gets him there on its own.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Jacksonville games have averaged 38.6 points, with four of five under. Its defense ranks 3rd in EPA and 3rd against the run, facing a Houston run game 26th in rush EPA that is likely without Montgomery. Houston's defense is no pushover either. An early London forecast shows gusts to 28, a hedge-level nudge.
picks.risk: Jacksonville's 7th-ranked pass offense meets a Houston secondary missing Pitre, and a couple of explosives blow past the number.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: The net EPA gap is wide (0.178, 3rd vs 0.019, 14th), as is the point-differential gap (+10.6 vs -0.4 a game). Houston's run game (26th in rush EPA) runs into a top-three run defense without its lead back, and its secondary loses a 92%-snap safety.
picks.risk: Houston's pass rush against a line that may be missing RT Harrison, plus a low total that makes 3 points a real hurdle; at Wembley there is little home field.

picks.label: Lawrence sacks taken
picks.case: Houston ranks 8th in QB-hit rate, and the report cites a top-three sack rate. Jacksonville allows hits at a high rate, and Lawrence turns 32% of pressures into sacks. His starting right tackle Harrison is questionable after leaving last game with a knee injury.
picks.risk: Houston's overall pressure rate is only 13th. If Harrison plays and Jacksonville leans on the run with a lead, the dropbacks shrink.

picks.bet: Stroud under his 1.2-a-game passing TD average (0 or 1)
picks.label: Stroud passing TDs
picks.case: Jacksonville allows one passing TD a game to quarterbacks, second-fewest, and has the 2nd-best red-zone defense. Houston converts 31.4% on third down, which stalls drives short of the red zone, and it fits the under consensus.
picks.risk: Jacksonville's starting safety Murray is out, and without a run game Houston may throw near the goal line.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Tampa's offense is 27th in EPA and 29th passing, and it is on backup Jalon Daniels, whose two starts totaled 31 and 40 points. Pittsburgh's pass offense is 26th and missing Pittman, Wilson and another receiver. Tampa's 5th-ranked defense and ball-control style shorten the game. An early forecast of 20 mph wind with 30 mph gusts would push further down if it holds.
picks.risk: Pittsburgh's last three went over, and its defense allows explosive passes.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: The efficiency gap is small (net EPA 20th vs 22nd). Tampa is home on 10 days' rest, and all four of its losses came within one score. Pittsburgh's passing game ranks 26th and is stripped of three receivers. In a 40.5-total game, three points is a real cushion.
picks.risk: Mayfield is out, and a Tampa offense ranked 29th passing may not score enough to stay within a field goal.

picks.label: Rodgers sacks taken
picks.case: His 2.8 sacks a game come mostly on shotgun third downs. Tampa ranks 29th in QB-hit rate, and the report cites a 28th-ranked sack rate. Pittsburgh's 4th-ranked rush offense and a possible windy day favor a run-leaning plan that limits dropbacks.
picks.risk: Rodgers' season average is already over the line, and a gutted receiver room makes holding the ball more likely.

picks.bet: Jalon Daniels under his 168.5-per-start passing average
picks.label: J. Daniels passing yards
picks.case: His passing is short and screen-heavy. Pittsburgh ranks 7th against short passes, per the report, and allows the 2nd-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks. A run-leaning Tampa script (7th in rush EPA) and an early wind forecast cap the volume.
picks.risk: A Pittsburgh lead forces Tampa to throw, inflating attempts.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: The efficiency gap (net EPA 0.063 vs 0.011; point differential +3.2 vs -0.6) supports a line nearer 4-5 than the hook past a touchdown. The Jets' defense ranks 7th, has the 2nd-best sack rate and has held four of five opponents to 23 or fewer. New England is without both 95%-snap corners, has a -1.0 turnover margin, and LT Campbell is questionable.
picks.risk: The Jets' offense is missing Hall, Mitchell and Parham and may not score enough to keep it inside a touchdown.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: The Jets score 18.6 a game and lose Hall, Mitchell and Parham against New England's 5th-ranked pass defense. Their own 7th-ranked defense and 7th-ranked run defense slow a Patriots ground game ranked 23rd. The Jets' scoring and points-allowed averages add to 37.8, and four of five Jets games went under.
picks.risk: New England's 9th-ranked pass offense hangs another big number (45 against the Raiders) on a Jets pass defense ranked 18th.

picks.label: Maye sacks taken
picks.case: Maye holds the ball over three seconds, and the Jets have the league's 2nd-best sack rate. His 87%-snap left tackle Campbell is questionable with a sprained knee.
picks.risk: The Jets rank 30th in pressure rate, so their sacks may not recur; a New England lead also cuts dropbacks.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: Both teams are poor by net EPA, but the Giants (24th) beat the Saints (27th) and are at home. New Orleans' 31st-ranked run defense is missing its 100%-snap linebacker Elliss and two interior linemen, which suits the league's most run-leaning offense. At 1.5, a win covers.
picks.risk: Both defenses are bad (22nd and 27th), so this is close to a coin flip decided by turnovers, where the Giants are only +0.2 a game.

picks.label: Shough sacks taken
picks.case: The Giants rank last in pressure rate, 28th in hit rate and 26th in sack rate, and just put edge rusher Golston on IR. Shough's pressure-to-sack rate has improved sharply.
picks.risk: A trailing script that piles up dropbacks, or Saints line issues, produces a couple of coverage sacks.

picks.bet: Giants over their season rushing-yards average
picks.label: Giants team rushing yards
picks.case: New York leans on the run more than almost anyone (pass rate over expected -9.1, 30th). The Saints rank 31st in rush EPA allowed, are missing Elliss and DTs Shepherd and Broughton, and just gave up 205 rushing yards to Atlanta and 153 to Minnesota.
picks.risk: The Giants' rushing efficiency is only 25th, and an early deficit would shift them to the pass.

picks.bet: Henry over his season rushing average
picks.label: Henry rushing yards
picks.case: Cleveland ranks 29th in rush EPA allowed and last in explosive runs. It has DTs Graham and Hall out and its 100%-snap linebacker Schwesinger questionable with an ankle sprain. With Jackson out, Baltimore leaned harder on Henry and ran for 208 yards against a top-10 defense, and the forecast is mild.
picks.risk: Center Jurgens is out. Cleveland's 4th-ranked pass defense could let it load the box against a backup QB without paying for it.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: The net EPA gap is wide (5th vs 23rd), and Cleveland's 3-2 rests on a -3.8 point differential and 1.26 wins over expectation. Baltimore already won by seven on the road with its backup. Henry against a depleted, 29th-ranked run defense is the path, and a Jackson return would be upside.
picks.risk: With Jackson, Jurgens and Hendrickson out, Baltimore's season numbers overstate this lineup. A low-total division game against a 4th-ranked pass defense can land inside 4.5.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Baltimore is likely on its backup QB, runs well below its expected pass rate (-6.0) and holds the ball about 32 minutes a game. Cleveland's offense scores 18.6 and ranks 31st in rush EPA. Both short-pass and red-zone defenses push drives toward field goals.
picks.risk: Henry breaks long runs against a defense last in explosive runs, or Watson hits deep shots on a 31st-ranked WR1 defense.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Titans games have averaged about 33 points, with four of five under, and this is the highest total they've faced. Tennessee's offense is 31st in EPA and runs heavily (-8.2 pass rate over expected). The Colts' pass offense is 29th and missing Pierce and other receivers. Both sides' run-heavy scripts shorten the game.
picks.risk: Indianapolis's 26th-ranked defense and 1st-ranked run game produce a lopsided score, as in the Colts' three overs.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: The spread and total imply about 18.75 for Tennessee, which averages a league-low 11.6 points. Its pass offense ranks 31st and its special teams are the worst. The Colts held the two mid-tier offenses they faced to 17 and 13.
picks.risk: Pollard and the run game shred the league's worst run defense, and Colts turnovers (-1.2 a game) hand Tennessee short fields.

picks.bet: Pollard over his season rushing average
picks.label: Pollard rushing yards
picks.case: Indianapolis is last in rush EPA allowed and last against lead backs (+5.8 PPR over average to RB1s), and it is missing edge rusher Key and LB Carlies. Tennessee's line has the league's lowest stuff rate per the report, and the Titans stay run-heavy (-8.2 pass rate over expected). Yards can come without points, so this fits the TEN team-total under.
picks.risk: An early deficit like Week 5 abandons the run.

picks.label: Jones passing TDs
picks.case: Jones has thrown zero or one TD pass in every game, 3 in 5. Tennessee holds TE1s 6.4 PPR under average (1st) and ranks 5th in fewest QB TDs allowed. As a 7-point favorite with the league's best rush EPA, Indy should hand red-zone work to the backs.
picks.risk: Tennessee's 27th-ranked pass defense is missing Hooker, with Winston and Flott hurt, which can hand out a couple of easy scores.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: Carolina ranks 8th in net EPA to Philadelphia's 30th, and its 6th-ranked pass offense meets a 24th-ranked pass defense with the 31st pressure rate and worst QB-hit rate, which covers Carolina's pass-protection weakness. Carolina comes off a bye (14 days' rest) against a team back from London. Philadelphia is missing center Kendall and the retired Lane Johnson, with Barkley and Smith out as of now. A near pick'em prices the jersey.
picks.risk: Sirianni is hopeful Barkley and Smith return, which would lift an offense ranked 29th, and Carolina's league-best +1.3 turnover margin may regress.

picks.label: Young passing yards
picks.case: He has cleared 287 in every game on 36-48 attempts, in the third-most pass-heavy offense (+5.9 pass rate over expected). Philadelphia ranks 24th in pass EPA and 31st in pressure rate, so he should have time.
picks.risk: An early lead in a 41.5-total game cuts his attempts, and WR Legette is on IR with Coker returning from injury.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: The line implies 21.5 for an offense averaging 18.4 and ranked 29th in EPA and 27th in rush EPA. It is short its center and right tackle and possibly its top receiver and back. Carolina has allowed under 17 a game outside a Week 1 outlier and ranks 4th in pressure rate.
picks.risk: Barkley and Smith both play, or Philadelphia's special teams and fourth-down aggression manufacture points.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: This is the highest total of either team's season; Atlanta's first five closed between 40.5 and 47.5, and Chicago's last four went under. Both rank top five in time of possession and run more than expected (pass rate over expected -3.1 and -9.0). Both quarterbacks, Williams and Penix, are uncertain, and the scoring averages point to about 45.
picks.risk: Chicago's 27th-ranked run defense lets Atlanta's 3rd-ranked run game rip off long drives that end in touchdowns, and the indoor setting removes weather help.

picks.bet: Bijan Robinson over his season rushing average
picks.label: Robinson rushing yards
picks.case: Atlanta has run for 110+ in every game regardless of quarterback, with Robinson at about 20 carries behind a run game ranked 3rd in rush EPA. Chicago is 27th in rush EPA allowed and 30th against lead backs, and Edwards and Odeyingbo are questionable.
picks.risk: If Atlanta falls behind early, or Penix's absence lets Chicago stack the box, his carries dip.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: The spread and total imply about 26.25 for Chicago, which has scored 3, 27, 23 and 7 since the opener. Atlanta's defense ranks 7th in EPA and, per the report, 3rd in success rate allowed and 5th in deep EPA. Williams' hamstring leaves Chicago's quarterback unsettled.
picks.risk: Williams returns and Atlanta turnovers (-1.0 a game) set up short fields.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: Net EPA has these teams nearly even (12th vs 15th), yet Chicago lays 3 on the road with Williams out as of now and a -1.2 turnover margin. Atlanta's 3rd-ranked run game meets the Bears' 27th-ranked run defense, with several Bears defenders questionable.
picks.risk: Penix's ribs: if he is ruled out, much of the edge goes, and a Williams return swings it the other way.

picks.label: Stafford passing TDs
picks.case: Arizona allows 3 TDs a game to quarterbacks and ranks 31st in pass EPA, with starting safety Wingard out. Stafford has 7 TDs on 28 red-zone throws, and his two games against bottom-ten defenses produced 4 and 3. It's indoors, and the Rams pass well above expectation (+4.0).
picks.risk: A big lead turns the second half over to the run game, leaving him at one.

picks.bet: Brissett over his 40-a-game pass attempts average
picks.label: Brissett pass attempts
picks.case: Arizona is a 13.5-point underdog against an offense that passes well above expectation, and its own pass defense ranks 31st. Brissett has already logged 85 dropbacks while trailing by 9+. A catch-up script means volume, indoors.
picks.risk: A line missing LT Johnson and G Adams gives up sacks and scrambles that don't count as attempts, as when Detroit sacked him five times.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: The implied 19.5 asks Arizona to score on a Rams defense ranked 2nd against TE1s and 4th against WR1s by EPA, which is where Arizona's volume goes, and the Rams lead the league against deep passes. Arizona just lost its left tackle and a guard, scored 7 against the one elite defense it faced, and took five sacks from Detroit in its first game without Johnson.
picks.risk: Garbage-time scores against a soft late-game defense, and the Rams' turnovers, can push Arizona past 19.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: Net EPA has these teams close (BUF 10th, LV 12th), and Buffalo's +4.6 point differential leans on a 0.75 one-score win rate; only two of its five results would have covered six. Buffalo's defense ranks 30th in EPA, while Las Vegas has the 2nd-ranked pressure rate and a top-10 pass offense at home. Moore, Palmer, Oliver and Alford are all out for Buffalo.
picks.risk: Buffalo's top-ranked offense runs away with it, as New England did against Las Vegas.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: The Raiders' 10th-ranked pass offense meets Buffalo's 29th-ranked pass defense, which ranks 27th on short throws and is without slot CB Alford and DT Oliver. Las Vegas averages 26.4 and Buffalo allows 28.2, with a red-zone defense ranked 27th or worse, indoors.
picks.risk: Las Vegas' 29th-ranked run game stalls drives, and a Buffalo pass rush ranked 7th in pressure forces field goals.

picks.label: Cousins passing yards
picks.case: Buffalo allows 314 passing yards a game (31st) and ranks 27th against short passes, Cousins' best area, with slot CB Alford out. A 53.5 total, a six-point deficit and a dome point to heavy volume.
picks.risk: A Raiders lead or a run-heavy plan trims attempts, and Buffalo's pressure rate (7th) disrupts him.

picks.label: Cousins passing TDs
picks.case: He has thrown 2+ TDs in four of five games, and Buffalo allows 2.6 passing TDs a game (28th) with a red-zone defense ranked 27th or worse. That offsets expected regression in his red-zone rate.
picks.risk: Red-zone trips that end in field goals or runs, and his red-zone rate regressing.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Buffalo games average 61 combined points (32.8 scored, 28.2 allowed), four of five went over, and the Raiders' last three totaled 62, 57 and 62. The league's top offense meets a defense ranked 29th on short passes, Buffalo's 30th-ranked defense faces a top-10 pass attack, and it's indoors.
picks.risk: The number is already high, and Buffalo is down Moore and Palmer at receiver with RT Brown questionable.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: The line implies about 17 for a Chargers offense that ranks last in EPA, has topped 17 once in five games with a full roster, and averaged 16.8. It is now without both tackles (Slater, Alt), two guards and receivers Johnston and likely Harris, with McConkey questionable. KC's top-10 defense and 5th-ranked red-zone defense (per the report) await, and an early gusty forecast leans the same way.
picks.risk: A Chargers defense ranked 6th creates turnovers and short fields, or garbage-time scores land late.

picks.label: Herbert passing yards
picks.case: He just threw for 121 yards, his top three wideouts are out, doubtful or questionable, and both tackles are out. The offense has the league's lowest pass rate over expected (-12.1), and KC ranks 6th in short-pass EPA and explosive pass rate allowed. An early forecast of 27 mph gusts would push it further.
picks.risk: A big deficit forces 40+ attempts, and garbage-time yardage lifts him over his average.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Four of five Chargers games went under. The offense ranks last in EPA, runs more than anyone and is missing most of its line and receivers. Its 6th-ranked defense keeps KC from cruising. An early forecast of 16 mph wind and 27 mph gusts adds a hedged nudge.
picks.risk: KC's 4th-ranked offense, rested off a bye with a top-two run game, can reach the low 30s alone.

picks.label: Mahomes passing yards
picks.case: The Chargers allow the 5th-fewest passing yards to quarterbacks and hold WR1s 7.4 PPR under average (2nd). A projected KC lead behind the 2nd-ranked rush offense means a run-heavy finish, Thornton is on IR, and early wind (gusts 27) would only help.
picks.risk: Rice returns healthy, and LA's 32nd-ranked defense against WR2s gets exploited before the game is decided.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: Kansas City is 2nd in net EPA and rested off a bye. It faces a 0-5 ATS Chargers team whose last-ranked offense has lost four starting linemen and most of its receivers. KC's two non-covers were shootouts against competent offenses, which this group isn't.
picks.risk: The Chargers' 6th-ranked defense and a low, possibly windy total keep the margin inside 8.5, and KC's sack rate is 31st, per the report.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Green Bay's games average 43.2 points and only one of five cleared this number. Its offense scores 20.8 a game with the league's worst rushing EPA and is missing center Monk. The Packers allow the 2nd-lowest explosive pass rate, so 52.5 leans on Dallas' shootout history. An early forecast of 19 mph wind with 39 mph gusts at Lambeau would push it further if it holds.
picks.risk: Dallas' last-ranked defense, without corners Durant and Porter, lets Love carve it up while Dallas' 4th-ranked offense keeps pace.

picks.bet: Kittle over his season receiving-yards average
picks.label: Kittle receiving yards
picks.case: Washington allows TE1s 10.7 PPR over their averages (32nd) and is missing three safeties, including its 99%-snap starter Cross. Deebo Samuel is out, which concentrates targets over the middle on Kittle, where Purdy produces 0.826 EPA a throw.
picks.risk: Juszczyk's return or a run-heavy blowout script spreads the work, or Kittle stays in to block.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: The net EPA gap is enormous (1st vs 25th). San Francisco's top-ranked pass offense faces a secondary missing three safeties and a starting corner. Washington is without Diggs and Mariota, and its offense is 27th in success rate, per the report. SF's home wins came by 22, 6 and 10.
picks.risk: SF is missing Sigle, Greenlaw, Samuel and possibly Bosa, with poor special teams, and +2.03 wins over expected; the hook past 7 is a real hurdle.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: The spread and total imply 29 for San Francisco, which averages 30.8. Washington allows 29.8 a game, ranks 25th in pass EPA and has the league's worst red-zone TD rate. Its pass rush is weak (27th in sack rate), giving Purdy a clean pocket.
picks.risk: Washington's 31-minute time of possession limits SF's drives; a push at 29 is possible.

picks.label: Purdy passing yards
picks.case: Washington allows 287.6 passing yards a game to QBs (28th) and is a strong pass funnel (+6.1 pass rate over expected allowed, 3rd) with a 7th-ranked run defense. Its secondary is missing three safeties and a starting corner. Santa Clara's early forecast (gusts 20) is not a concern.
picks.risk: A big early lead turns the second half to McCaffrey, and Samuel's absence thins his options.
